sections.title: IMPORTANT - NEW UPDATE
sections.description:
Hi Team,

This week we're kicking off a new training block instead of our traditional transition week. 
The reason is that we're introducing a new program structure to complement the format we've been using over the past year. Because this new design provides a different training stimulus than what you have been used to, it serves the same purpose as a traditional transition week.
That said, make sure to ease into Week 1 of this new block. Give your body time to adapt to the new structure before increasing the intensity and loads. From Week 2 onwards, you can begin ramping things up.

For more than a year, we've used our highly effective Heavy/Light design (Alt. between Strength/WL days and Gym/Conditioning days). In this block, we're introducing a new approach: an Upper/Lower design (Alt. between Upper-body and Lower-body biased sessions/days).

Going forward, we'll alternate between our Heavy/Light design and the Upper/Lower design from block to block (4 weeks per block). 
By undulating between these two systems, we expose you to a different training stimuli, continue driving progress, reduce the risk of stagnation, and build the most well-rounded fitness possible. The goal is simple: to help you keep improving as quickly as possible while making that progress sustainable over the long term.

So to nail this first week, make sure that intensity is self-regulated. 
If you feel great, push. If you don’t, dial it back.
_______________________
Have a great training week!
– André Houdet
nst

sections.title: NEW TRAINING BLOCK W1/4
sections.description:
Welcome to week 1 of our new training block Team,
If you just joined the team, make sure to read below:

I encourage you to watch the block explanation video below that will give you a deep insight into how the program is structured from a macro to micro level (Global-->Weekly-->Daily overview). 
Video link (block explanation): https://youtu.be/qGrVz4srDHw

If you do not have the time to watch the block explanation video, you can as always read the detailed notes attached in each section of the program to understand the intent behind everything. Due to FITr's layout, we have added the text as attachments to have less text in each box.

Our goal with this training program is to have you feel:
a. Constant progress through consistent good training weeks.
b. Feeling good (injury free)
c. Motivated and driven as you see and understand the intention of how the program is structured.

Our training principles to have success with the program:
#1 If you want to be good at something, you must above all else,
be consistent.
#2 Minimum Effective dose: This is a principle that we use to underline the concept of more frequent good training sessions leads to better results long term. Often if we train too hard we also need a longer recovery time before we can train hard again. Rather keep 5% in the tank instead of overreaching. Typically, people who do not take the needed recovery time from the sessions where they did more than they should end up injured/hits a plateau. We do not need to go to the maximum every time to create adaptation. 
#3 Self-regulation: Listen to your body and adjust the intensity based on how you feel.
#4 Consistently good rather than occasionally great: Many good sessions are always better than a few great. 
#5 The devil is in the detail: Be deliberate and pay attention to set up/reps/tempo/intensity described in the program. 
#6 Stay in your lane: Don’t get caught up in anybody else’s game, you focus on you and your progress.
#7 Technique > Load
#8 Quality > Quantity
#9 Principles > Methods
--------------------------------------
Have a great training block team,
/𝙰𝚗𝚍𝚛𝚎 𝙷𝚘𝚞𝚍𝚎𝚝
𝙳𝚒𝚛𝚎𝚌𝚝𝚘𝚛 𝚘𝚏 𝚃𝚛𝚊𝚒𝚗𝚒𝚗𝚐.
𝚗𝚜𝚝.

sections.title: S1: ABSOLUTE STRENGTH (Press)
sections.description:
Absolute Strength, Anterior Upper-body (Press)

a. Build to a 5RM Bench press

b. 3 sets, Going every 3rd minute
Set 1: 5 Bench press at 85% of 5RM
Set 2: 5 Bench press at 85% of 5RM
Set 3: Max Bench press at 85% of 5RM

Tempo: Controlled decent, As aggressive and strong upwards as possible. Rest as needed in the top. (20X1)

Optional -- > Bands / Chains (accomodating resistance): If you’re up for it and have access to either 1-2 bands or chains, I’d recommend incorporating accommodating resistance. It’s an effective tool for addressing sticking points and creating a more even resistance profile throughout the lift. This matches the strength curve - making the lift harder where you are strongest (the top) and lighter where you are weakest (the bottom). 
Bands/chains are not mandatory though, so no stress if you don't want to bother setting it up.

Progression:
W1: 5RM Bench press + 5/5/5+ at 85% of 5RM (current)
W2: 3RM Bench press + 3/3/3+ at 85% of 3RM
W3: 1RM Bench press + 1/1/1+ at 85% of 1RM
W4: Transition week.
----------------------------------
Read more about how strength is developed in our program in attached document.

sections.title: S1: STRENGTH ENDURANCE (Press/Pull)
sections.description:
Strength Endurance, Anterior + Posterior Upper-body (Press/Pull)

a. 4 sets,
8 Strict Pull ups
-Rest 90 sec-
8 Strict Ring Dips
-Rest 90 sec-

Difficulty level:
[Elite] Add load via weight belt attachment or weighted vest.
[RX] Body weight.
[Intermediate] Band Assisted Strict pull ups and dips.

Tempo: Quality and control is key.

Intent: Improve muscle endurance and strength qualities in pressing and pulling exercises.
----------------------------------
Read more about how strength is developed in our program in attached document.

sections.title: S1: RELATIVE STRENGTH ENDURANCE / GYMNASTICS (Press)
sections.description:
(Relative) Strength Endurance / Gymnastics, Press (Drop set)

Elite:
a. 4 sets,
A “tough” set of Strict HSPU
-Into-
A “tough” set of Banded Seated shoulder press*
-Into-
A “Max” set of Banded tricep extensions
-3 minute rest-

RX:
a. 4 sets,
A “tough” set of Strict HSPU (Elevated head with 1x abmat + 0-2x10kg plates to get more than 8 each time if needed)
-Into-
A “tough” set of Banded Seated shoulder press*
-Into-
A “Max” set of Banded tricep extensions
-3 minute rest-

Intermediate:
a. 4 sets,
A “tough” set of Pike HSPU (Hands on plates to create deficit if you are at ease)
-Into-
A “tough” set of Banded Seated shoulder press*
-Into-
A “Max” set of Banded tricep extensions
-3 minute rest-

*Alternative (if you struggle to set this up): Seated Double DB Strict press Pick a weight where you can do 10+ reps each time. Suggested loads are around: 2x15/10kg - 2x35/25lbs

A "Tough" set: Stop 2-4 reps before failure.

A "Max" set: Go to failure.

Drop set intent:
Accumulate a high volume of pressing work by progressively reducing the mechanical demands of the movement while continuing to fatigue the same primary muscle groups. This allows us to build strength-endurance, increase hypertrophy, and improve fatigue resistance in gymnastics pressing movements effectively. 
----------------------------------
Read more about how endurance and gymnastics is developed in our program in attached document.

sections.title: S1: CONDITIONING (Threshold)
sections.description:
Conditioning, “Raising the ceiling” (Threshold intervals │ 75-85% effort │ Heavy-Severe intensity domain)

Elite:
a. In a 20 minute window complete as many sets as possible of:
60 Double Unders* 
6 Lengths Farmer carry (1 length: 25ft/7.6m)
6 Bar Muscle ups
Rest 1 minute after each round
♀ 2x22.5kg │ 2x50lbs
♂ 2x32.5kg │ 2x70lbs
(*Use a "Beaded" rope if you have that available)

RX:
a. In a 20 minute window complete as many sets as possible of:
50 Double Unders
4 Lengths Farmer carry (1 length: 25ft/7.6m)
3 Bar Muscle ups
Rest 1 minute after each round
♀ 2x22.5kg │ 2x50lbs
♂ 2x32.5kg │ 2x70lbs

Intermediate:
a. In a 20 minute window complete as many sets as possible of:
60 Single Unders
6 Lengths Farmer carry (1 length: 25ft/7.6m)
6 Kipping Chest to bar
Rest 1 minute after each round
♀ 2x15kg │ 2x35lbs
♂ 2x22.5kg │ 2x50lbs

Scaled:
(Option #1)
In a 20 minute window complete as many sets as possible of:
60 Single Unders
6 Lengths Farmer carry (1 length: 25ft/7.6m)
6 Kipping Pull ups
Rest 1 minute after each round
♀ 2x15kg │ 2x35lbs
♂ 2x22.5kg │ 2x50lbs

(Option #2)
Spend 20 minutes learning Bar Muscle ups using the progressions found in the attached files.

Score: Total number of reps accumulated within the 20 minute window (Make sure to put a comment with what level you completed the workout at)

Flow explained: (Elite example)
60 Double unders, 6 lengths farmer carry, 6 BMU, Rest 1 minute. Repeat for as many rounds as possible until the 20 minutes are up.
---------------------------------
Read more about how endurance and gymnastics is developed in our program in attached document.

sections.title: S1: (OPTIONAL) STRENGTH ACCESSORY
sections.description:
(Optional) Strength Accessory

a.  2-3 sets for quality: (rest as needed between)
A “Max” set of Incline DB bicep curls (2x10-15/6-10kg - 2x25-35/15-25lbs)
A “Max” set of Banded Anchored sit ups

sections.title: S2: CONDITIONING
sections.description:
Conditioning, Run (Threshold)

a. Warm up 
10 min Easy Jog
-Into-
3 sets, 15 sec Strides* / 45 sec Walk

*Strides are a few short, progressive accelerations to “wake up” your legs and nervous system before the main workout, fast but relaxed, with full recovery.

b. Main set
5km completed as:
2 min Run ("Moderate-Hard" / Threshold / RPE 7-8 / Z4 / 10-20 sec slower than target 5k min/km pace)
-1 min Walk between-

c. Cool down
5-10 minute Easy Jog/Walk

Progression: (Threshold Density progression)
W1: 5km completed as:
2 min Run ("Moderate-Hard" / Threshold / RPE 7-8 / Z4 / 10-20 sec slower than target 5k pace)
-1 min Walk between-
W2:  5km completed as:
3 min Run ("Moderate-Hard" / Threshold / RPE 7-8 / Z4 / 10-20 sec slower than target 5k pace)
-1 min Walk between-
W3: 5km completed as:
4 min Run ("Moderate-Hard" / Threshold / RPE 7-8 / Z4 / 10-20 sec slower than target 5k pace)
-1 min Walk between-
W4: Transition week.
---------------------------------
Read more about how endurance and gymnastics is developed in our program in attached document.
